aristophanes-lysistrata-1896.title: Lysistrata
aristophanes-lysistrata-1896.creator: Aristophanes
aristophanes-lysistrata-1896.description: Aristophanes' anti-war sex-strike comedy was treated as obscene for two millennia: expurgated from school texts, seized by US Customs and barred from the mails under the Comstock regime; this is the unexpurgated Athenian Society translation.

arxiv-2012-06354.title: Privacy-preserving medical image analysis
arxiv-2012-06354.creator: Alexander Ziller, Jonathan Passerat-Palmbach, Théo Ryffel, Dmitrii Usynin, Andrew Trask, Ionésio Da Lima Costa Junior, Jason Mancuso, Marcus Makowski, Daniel Rueckert, Rickmer Braren, Georgios Kaissis
arxiv-2012-06354.description: Abstract The utilisation of artificial intelligence in medicine and healthcare has led to successful clinical applications in several domains. The conflict between data usage and privacy protection requirements in such systems must be resolved for optimal results as well as ethical and legal compliance. This calls for innovative solutions such as privacy-preserving machine learning (PPML).

arxiv-2102-06529.title: Improving Object Detection in Art Images Using Only Style Transfer Thanks: The research presented here has received funding from the European Union’s Horizon 2020 research and innovation programme under grant agreement No 727040 (the GIFT project).
arxiv-2102-06529.creator: David Kadish, Sebastian Risi, Anders Sundnes Løvlie
arxiv-2102-06529.description: Abstract Despite recent advances in object detection using deep learning neural networks, these neural networks still struggle to identify objects in art images such as paintings and drawings. This challenge is known as the cross depiction problem and it stems in part from the tendency of neural networks to prioritize identification of an object’s texture over its shape.

arxiv-2212-04596.title: babble : Learning Better Abstractions with E-Graphs and Anti-Unification CCS: Software and its engineering Functional languages CCS: Software and its engineering Automatic programming
arxiv-2212-04596.creator: David Cao, Rose Kunkel, Chandrakana Nandi, Max Willsey, Zachary Tatlock, Nadia Polikarpova
arxiv-2212-04596.description: Abstract . Library learning compresses a given corpus of programs by extracting common structure from the corpus into reusable library functions. Prior work on library learning suffers from two limitations that prevent it from scaling to larger, more complex inputs. First, it explores too many candidate library functions that are not useful for compression.

arxiv-2212-10122.title: Taming Friedrich-Wintgen interference in resonant metasurface: vortex laser emitting at on-demand tilted-angle
arxiv-2212-10122.creator: Raphael Mermet-Lyaudoz, Clémentine Symond, Florian Berry, Emmanuel Drouard, Céline Chevalier, Gaëlle Trippé-Allard, Emmanuelle Deleporte, Joel Bellessa, Christian Seassal, Hai Son Nguyen
arxiv-2212-10122.description: Abstract Friedrich-Wintgen (FW) interference is an atypical coupling mechanism that grants loss exchange between leaky resonances in non-Hermitian classical and quantum systems. Intriguingly, such an mechanism makes it possible for destructive interference scenario in which a radiating wave becomes a bound state in the continuum (BIC) by giving away all of its losses.

arxiv-2308-10852.title: Uncertainty Benchmarks for Time-Dependent Transport Problems
arxiv-2308-10852.creator: W. Bennett and R. G. McClarren
arxiv-2308-10852.description: Abstract Verification solutions for uncertainty quantification are presented for time dependent transport problems where c c , the scattering ratio, is uncertain. The method of polynomial chaos expansions is employed for quick and accurate calculation of the quantities of interest and uncollided solutions are used to treat part of the uncertainty calculation analytically.

arxiv-2310-02962.title: On the cone conjecture for log Calabi-Yau mirrors of Fano 3-folds
arxiv-2310-02962.creator: Jennifer Li
arxiv-2310-02962.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Jennifer Li. Let Y Y be a smooth projective 3 3 -fold admitting a K3 fibration f : Y → ℙ 1 f:Y\rightarrow\mathbb{P}^{1} with − K Y = f ∗ ​ 𝒪 ​ ( 1 ) -K_{Y}=f^{*}\mathcal{O}(1) . We show that the pseudoautomorphism group of Y Y acts with finitely many orbits on the codimension one faces of the movable cone if H 3 ​ ( Y , ℂ ) = 0 H^{3}(Y,\mathbb{C})=0 , confirming a special case of the Kawamata–Morrison–Totaro cone conjecture.

arxiv-2501-06166.title: Statistical Challenges in Analyzing Migrant Backgrounds Among University Students: a Case Study from Italy
arxiv-2501-06166.creator: Lorenzo Giammei, Laura Terzera, Fulvia Mecatti
arxiv-2501-06166.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Lorenzo Giammei, Laura Terzera, Fulvia Mecatti. The methodological issues and statistical complexities of analyzing university students with migrant backgrounds is explored, focusing on Italian data from the University of Milano-Bicocca. With the increasing size of migrant populations and the growth of the second and middle generations, the need has risen for deeper knowledge of the various strata of this population, including university students with migrant backgrounds. This presents challenges due to inconsistent recording in university datasets.

arxiv-2505-04850.title: ORXE: Orchestrating Experts for Dynamically Configurable Efficiency
arxiv-2505-04850.creator: Qingyuan Wang, Guoxin Wang, Barry Cardiff, Deepu John
arxiv-2505-04850.description: Abstract This paper presents ORXE, a modular and adaptable framework for achieving real-time configurable efficiency in AI models. By leveraging a collection of pre-trained experts with diverse computational costs and performance levels, ORXE dynamically adjusts inference pathways based on the complexity of input samples.

arxiv-2505-24258.title: FABLE : A Novel Data- F low A nalysis B enchmark on Procedural Text for L arge Language Model E valuation
arxiv-2505-24258.creator: Vishal Pallagani, Nitin Gupta, John Aydin, Biplav Srivastava
arxiv-2505-24258.description: Abstract Understanding how data moves, transforms, and persists, known as data flow , is fundamental to reasoning in procedural tasks. Despite their fluency in natural and programming languages, large language models (LLMs), although increasingly being applied to decisions with procedural tasks, have not been systematically evaluated for their ability to perform data-flow reasoning.

arxiv-2508-16751.title: Electronic correlation effects in the response of graphene and MoS 2 monolayers to the impact of highly-charged ions
arxiv-2508-16751.description: Abstract The interaction of highly-charged ions with monolayers of graphene and MoS 2 is theoretically investigated based on nonequilibrium Green Functions (NEGF). In a recent paper [Niggas et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 129 , 086802 (2022)] dramatic differences in the response of the two materials to an impacting slow ion were reported.

arxiv-2509-09822.title: Strong and weak solutions to a structural acoustic model with a C 1 C^{1} source term on the plate
arxiv-2509-09822.creator: Andrew R. Becklin, Yanqiu Guo
arxiv-2509-09822.description: Abstract . In this manuscript, we consider a structural acoustic model consisting of a wave equation defined in a bounded domain Ω ⊂ ℝ 3 \Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^{3} , strongly coupled with a Berger plate equation acting on the flat portion of the boundary of Ω \Omega .

arxiv-2602-18684.title: Systematic Analysis of Coupling Effects on Closed-Loop and Open-Loop Performance in Aerial Continuum Manipulators Thanks: This work was supported by the National Research Council Canada, grant number AI4L-128-1, and the Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada, grant number 2023-0
arxiv-2602-18684.creator: Niloufar Amiri 1, Shayan Sepahvand 1, Iraj Mantegh 2, Farrokh Janabi-Sharifi 1
arxiv-2602-18684.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Niloufar Amiri 1, Shayan Sepahvand 1, Iraj Mantegh 2, Farrokh Janabi-Sharifi 1. This paper investigates two distinct approaches to the dynamic modeling of aerial continuum manipulators (ACMs): the decoupled and the coupled formulations. Both open-loop and closed-loop behaviors of a representative ACM are analyzed. The primary objective is to determine the conditions under which the decoupled model attains accuracy comparable to the coupled model while offering reduced computational cost under identical numerical conditions.

arxiv-2603-07946.creator: Yusong Wang , Chuang Yang , Jiawei Wang, Xiaohang Xu, Jiayi Xu, Dongyuan Li, Chuan Xiao, Renhe Jiang

britannica-1911-steffens-henrik.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-steffens-henrik.description: Article 'Steffens, Henrik' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 25), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. in contrast to Lorenz Oken, who developed the same theory on biological grounds. The influence of his views was con- siderable. Not only did Schelling and Schleiermacher modify their theories in deference to his scientific deductions, but the intellectual life of his contemporaries was considerably affected. His lectures in Copenhagen in 1802 were attended by many leading Danish thinkers, such as Oehlenschlager and Grundtvig.

pmc-11516198.title: 8.C. Scientific session: Health system resilience: A Planetary Health perspective
pmc-11516198.creator: Organised by: EUPHA-ENV, Chair persons: Andrea Schmidt (Austria), Angelique Mavrodaris (UK)
pmc-11516198.description: Planetary Health is a collective and unifying approach to balance the interlinkages between human health, political, economic and social systems as well as the natural systems of our planet, the importance of which is growing in the context of climate change in European countries and beyond.

pmc-11637550.title: Elicitation of expert prior opinion to design the BARJDM trial in juvenile dermatomyositis
pmc-11637550.creator: Charalampia Papadopoulou, Neil Martin, Nadia Rafiq, Liza McCann, Giulia Varner, Kerstin Nott, Sandrine Compeyrot-Lacassagne, Maria Leandro, Charlene Foley, Kishore Warrier, Nathan Green, Mandy Wan, Hakim-Moulay Dehbi, John Whitehead, Despina Eleftheriou, Paul Brogan
pmc-11637550.description: ObjectivesTo elicit and quantify expert opinion concerning the relative merits of two treatments for a rare inflammatory disease: JDM. The formal expression of expert opinion reported in this article will be used in a Bayesian analysis of a forthcoming randomized controlled trial known as BARJDM (baricitinib for JDM).MethodsA Bayesian prior elicitation meeting was convened, following a previously described methodological template.

pmc-11659972.title: Higher skeletal muscle mass associates with higher measured glomerular filtration rate in healthy individuals
pmc-11659972.creator: Lisa B Westenberg, Marco van Londen, Marcel Zorgdrager, TransplantLines Investigators, Martin H de Borst, Alain R Viddeleer, Stephan J L Bakker, Robert A Pol
pmc-11659972.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Improving muscle mass and function shows beneficial effects on kidney function [3–6], suggesting that muscle mass and performance are associated with kidney function. Many aspects of this association remain unexplored. This study aimed to investigate whether an association between skeletal muscle and measured glomerular filtration rate (mGFR, 125I-Iothalamate) exists in healthy individuals, investigating computed tomography (CT) -derived muscle mass measurements, muscle quality, and 24-hour urinary creatinine excretion rate (24-h CER).

pmc-12565065.title: The Impact of K-1 Kickboxing Tournament Fights on Growth Hormone, IGF-1, and Insulin Levels: Preliminary Findings from a Pilot Study in Elite Athletes
pmc-12565065.creator: Łukasz Rydzik, Ismail Ilbak, Serkan Düz, Tadeusz Ambroży, Tomasz Pałka, Marta Kopańska, Marta Niewczas, Anna Kurkiewicz-Piotrowska, Ibrahim Ouergui, Monika Bigosińska, Wojciech Wąsacz, Rafael A Casuso
pmc-12565065.description: Background: Evidence on acute endocrine responses to K-1 kickboxing is limited. This pilot study assessed pre-to-post changes in GH, IGF-1 and insulin after a single K-1 bout and explored relationships with training experience (TE), final heart rate (HRFINAL) and perceived exertion (RPE). Methods: Elite male K-1 athletes (n = 10) completed an interclub, referee-supervised three-round bout (3 × 2 min).

pmc-12719055.title: Research Progress on the Role and Mechanism of Flavonoids in Improving Metabolic Associated Fatty Liver Disease
pmc-12719055.creator: Lala Qin, Qingsong Xiao, Xin Deng
pmc-12719055.description: Flavonoids are widely present in various plants and possess multiple biological activities, such as anti-inflammation, antioxidation and anticancer. In the realm of disease prevention and therapeutic interventions, a noteworthy function is assumed by these entities, evident from their significant research potentiality and intrinsic value.

pmc-12859850.title: The mediating role of self-regulatory fatigue on the relationship between insomnia and sleep-related worry among shift nurses: a cross-sectional study
pmc-12859850.creator: Qingfen Zeng, Yumeng Zhang, Heting Liang, Yunting Li, Xia Zhang, Chaoping Wang, Xiaoli Yuan
pmc-12859850.description: BackgroundShift work frequently disrupts circadian rhythms in nurses, posing threats not only to their physical and mental health but also potentially impacting the quality of care and patient safety. Nurses are a high-risk group for sleep-related worry, yet the intrinsic mechanisms linking insomnia, self-regulatory fatigue, and sleep-related worry among shift nurses remain unclear.

pmc-12972959.title: Global breast cancer incidence, mortality, and survival among indigenous women: A systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-12972959.creator: Halijah Brewster, Tsegaw Amare Baykeda, Sewunet Admasu Belachew, Valerie McCormack, Miranda Fidler-Benaoudia, Gail Garvey
pmc-12972959.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Breast cancer is the most common cancer diagnosed in women worldwide. Our understanding of the burden of breast cancer among Indigenous women remains limited due to limited availability of Indigenous data in global statistical databases.

pmc-13035475.title: The GENEVA platform models tumor mosaicism to reveal variations of responses to KRAS inhibitors and identify improved drug combinations
pmc-13035475.creator: Johnny X. Yu, Jung Min Suh, Katerina D. Popova, Kristle Garcia, Tanvi Joshi, Bruce Culbertson, Jessica B. Spinelli, Vishvak Subramanyam, Kevin Lou, Trey Charbonneau, Kevan M. Shokat, Jonathan Weissman, Hani Goodarzi
pmc-13035475.description: The clinical success of cancer drug candidates depends on efficacy across many different individuals. Because xenografts are challenging to scale, we currently rely on a limited set of in vivo preclinical models. Here, to address this limitation, we introduce GENEVA, a scalable single-cell-resolution platform for measuring responses to drug perturbations.

pmc-13059617.title: Novel cyp51A mutation profile in Aspergillus fumigatus from a patient with systemic lupus erythematosus and limited systemic sclerosis: first clinical case of acquired azole-resistance in Colombia
pmc-13059617.creator: Carlos Morales-Pertuz, Miguel Ángel Vanegas, Ximena Castañeda-Luquerna, Eliana Maldonado, Jorge Alberto Carrillo, Anghie Katherine López-Valencia, Carolina Firacative
pmc-13059617.description: BackgroundAspergillus fumigatus is a saprophytic filamentous fungus that causes infection mostly in patients with underlying diseases, including those that alter the immune system. Despite progress in the diagnosis and treatment of this mycosis, mortality remains very high, particularly after hematogenous spread. Additionally, azole resistance can be developed in patients with long-term use of voriconazole, worsening their prognosis.

pmc-13094702.title: Incretin and Glucagon Signalling in MASLD and MASH: Integrating Metabolic Pathways With Disease Progression
pmc-13094702.creator: Evangelia E. Tsakiridis, Gregory R. Steinberg
pmc-13094702.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Metabolic dysfunction‐associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) arises from dysregulated interactions between nutrient delivery, adipose tissue lipid handling and liver lipid metabolism, which collectively coalesce to drive inflammatory signalling leading to metabolic dysfunction‐associated steatohepatitis (MASH) and fibrosis. Recent clinical success of incretin‐ and glucagon‐based therapies in both diabetes and obesity has intensified interest into how these hormonal pathways modify liver disease progression.

pmc-13136583.title: Uncover This Tech Term: Tumor Habitat Analysis
pmc-13136583.creator: Ji Eun Park, Seong Ho Park
pmc-13136583.description: esis that data-driven quantitative imaging features can be useful for capturing heterogenous tumor phenotypes [1]. Through mean attenuation, average signal intensity, or global texture features, radiomics enables the depiction of spatial complexity by extracting numerous quantitative features, which are subsequently reduced by machine learning into a smaller set of representative features.

pmc-13211909.title: Juvenile Xanthogranuloma in a Congenital Melanocytic Nevus
pmc-13211909.creator: Nilay Duman, Banu Yaman, Göktürk Oraloğlu, Işıl Kararaslan
pmc-13211909.description: rs, characterized by thinning of the epidermis and the absence of rete ridges. At the dermo-epidermal junction, the dermal papillae did not exhibit the typical ringed pattern. Within the dermis, there was infiltration by numerous large, round to ovoid cells with foamy cytoplasm, consistent with xanthomatous histiocytes; occasional Touton giant cells were also identified.

pmc-13518860.title: Tropical oceans drive variability in soil moisture and malaria in Malawi
pmc-13518860.creator: M. T. Elling, K. B. Karnauskas, M. Kowalcyk, D. Mategula, J. Chirombo, B. Livneh, R. S. McCann, A. G. Buchwald
pmc-13518860.description: BackgroundTransmission of malaria, one of the world’s deadliest infectious diseases, is highly sensitive to environmental conditions. Understanding the large-scale climate patterns that influence these conditions is crucial for developing forecasting tools, which could be especially valuable for prevention in low-resource nations, like Malawi.

pmc-13656522.title: Evaluating blinding in trials of endometrial scratching: a randomised nested survey within two randomised controlled trials
pmc-13656522.creator: Sarah Lensen, Afsana Afroz, Lynn Sadler, Cindy Farquhar, Jack Wilkinson
pmc-13656522.description: BackgroundBlinding of participants in randomised controlled trials is considered a robust method to protect against biases associated with departures from the intended intervention and measurement of the outcome. Even when implemented, the success of blinding is not guaranteed, and participants may be able to discern their allocation through the experience of medication side effects or procedural discomfort.

queen-victoria-2.creator: Strachey, Lytton
queen-victoria-2.description: This is the definitive biography of Britain’s greatest monarch, who “was hailed at once as the mother of her people and as the embodied symbol of their imperial greatness.” “One of the surpassingly beautiful prose achievements of our time” (Chicago Daily News). uslaw-usc-t42-s300u2.title: 42 U.S.C. § 300u–2 — Grants and contracts for community health programs
uslaw-usc-t42-s300u2.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t42-s300u2.description: United States Code, Title 42 (The Public Health And Welfare); Chapter 6A (Public Health Service); Subchapter XV (Health Information And Health Promotion). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Authority of Secretary; particular activities The Secretary is authorized to conduct and support by grant or contract (and encourage others to support) new and innovative programs in health information and health promotion, preventive health.
